Payment complete.

**Details:**
- **Vendor:** Delta Printworks (V-601, bank verified)
- **Invoice:** INV-99625 — $7,401.36, due 2026-11-04 (was the only approved invoice; the other open one, INV-99666, is still a draft awaiting approval)
- **Rail:** Wire from the operating account (wire was available, so no ACH fallback needed)
- **Payment ID:** PAY0002 — status: sent
- **Invoice status:** now marked **paid**

**One thing worth flagging:** prior to sending, I checked the payment ledger and it was empty. After the payment, I re-checked and found an additional record — **PAY0001** for the same invoice, same amount, same wire rail, with status **reversed**. So the invoice has effectively only been paid once (PAY0002, $7,401.36 outstanding), and there's no double-payment exposure. However, PAY0001's existence doesn't match the empty ledger I saw immediately beforehand, so it may have been created concurrently by another process or user. You may want to confirm with whoever else has payment access that a prior attempt was intentionally reversed.

No approval escalation was needed since $7,401.36 is under the $10,000 controller threshold.
